<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par120 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=4}}.—A perfect is possibly subordinated in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=10}}; but the explanation of {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫אוּ}} as a relative clause is preferable.

{{GHGmargin-letter|120|d}}
'''2.''' Instead of subordination (as in the cases mentioned in ''a''–''c''), the ''co-ordination'' of the complementary verbal idea in the finite verb (cf. above, ''c'') frequently occurs, either—

(''a'') With the second verb co-ordinated in a form exactly corresponding to the first (but see below, ''e'') by means of {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָ}}).<ref>Cf. the English colloquial expression ''I will try and do it''.</ref> As a rule, here also (see above, ''a'') the principal idea is introduced only by the second verb, while the first (especially {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף}}<ref>Of a different kind are the cases in which {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף}} with a negative is co-ordinated with a verb to emphasize the non-recurrence of the action; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} ''they prophesied and added not'', sc. ''to prophesy'', i.e. ''but they did so no more''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19}} (reading {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא יֹאסִיף}}).</ref>, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹסִיף}}) contains the definition of the manner of the action, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫שָׁב וַיַּחְפֹּר|translate=and he returned and digged}}, i.e. he digged again; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=11}}, 13; in the perfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=13}}; with {{GHGheb|text=הוֹסִיף}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=1}} ''and Abraham added and took a wife'', i.e. again took a wife; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=5}} and frequently; with {{GHGheb|text=הוֹאִיל}} in the jussive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=9}}; in the imperative (cf. {{GHGpar|110|h}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹאֶל־נָא וְלִין|translate=be content, I pray thee, and tarry all night}} (cf. the English ''he was persuaded and remained'', for ''to remain''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=7|verse=29}}; with {{GHGheb|text=מִהֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=18}}, 20, &c.; with {{GHGheb|text=חִמַּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|120|e}}
Rem. 1. Instead of an exact agreement between co-ordinate verbal forms, other combinations sometimes occur, viz. imperfect and perfect consecutive (cf. {{GHGpar|112|d}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=12}} ''that they'' {{GHGheb|text=יִלְמְדוּ וְיָרְֽאוּ אֶת־יְהֹוָה|translate=may learn, and fear the Lord}}, i.e. ''to fear the Lord''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=25}}b; perfect and imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=3}} (''O that I knew how I might find him''); perfect and imperfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=1}}, 7; jussive and imperative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=10}}; cf., finally, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם־יָדַ֫עְתָּ וְיֶשׁ־בָּם|translate=and if thou knowest and there are among them}}, &c., i.e. that there are among them.

{{GHGmargin-letter|120|f}}
2. Special mention must be made of the instances in which the natural complement of the first verb is suppressed, or is added immediately after in the form of an historical statement, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25}} ''then Joseph commanded and they filled''<ref>Cf. the analogous examples in Kautzsch’s {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Bibl. Aram.}}, § 102.</ref> (prop. that they should fill, and they filled...; cf. the full form of expression in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=2}}); a further command is then added by means of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} and the infinitive; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=6}}; another instance of the same kind is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=27}} ''I have divined and the Lord hath blessed me'', &c., i.e. that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake.

{{GHGmargin-letter|120|g}}
(''b'') With the second verb (which, according to the above, represents the principal idea) attached ''without the copula''<ref>To be distinguished, of course, from the cases in which two equally important and independent verbs are used together without the copula in vigorous poetic imagery, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=8}}, &c.</ref> in the same mood, &c. In this construction (cf. {{GHGpar|110|h}}) the imperatives {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}} ({{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמִי}},<section end=par120 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
